title: XP Just bought XP , won't open

posts.author: UneaseTrash
posts.body:
I've been wanting to work with RPG maker for a while now and two days ago I saw it was on sale. I bought it off steam and when I tried to open the program it shows it loading for a second and then closed itself.
I'm using a surface pro 7 with windows 11 on it.
I have tried everything I could find online. Uninstall/reinstall, restart device, admirative mode, compatibility mode, changed my settings and aspect ratio, shut off my firewall and whitelisted the app, and a bunch more.
I'm completely out of ideas. If anyone has any idea how to make it work, I would appreciate it so much!
(Also, the free trial version off the RPGMaker website won't open either)

posts.author: kyonides
posts.body:
The other day someone had some activation issue and I told him that the web browser should have the TLS 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 or even 1.3 protocols activated, IIRC. Have you tried that already?
And where did you buy it? On Komodo Plaza? Or Steam?
If you bought it on KP, you can enter the same key on Steam and it will add it to your list in no time. The Steam version gotta run normally.
Note: Never post your RM product key online.

posts.author: UneaseTrash
posts.body:
I bought it from steam.
I just activated all the TLS and it still didn't work.
Thanks for trying to help. I really appreciate it.

posts.author: UneaseTrash
posts.body: Is there any chance my computer just doesn't support the app?

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
Considering you tested both the trial version and the Steam version, the issue can't be with the firewall or anything like that. It's probably related to the fact that it was developed for x32 processors.
This isn't a solution, just a way to try to isolate the issue:
Try running it in compatibility mode with Windows XP SP2 or Windows 7.
You will need to go to the folder where it is installed and right-click to open the properties and change

posts.body:
For what it's worth, I was able to install RMXP without any issue on my Windows 11 laptop a few months ago--so it definitely
can
be done...the question is just
how.
I know you said you tried uninstalling/reinstalling and running compatibility mode, Unease, but did you try running the installer in compatibility mode, not just the program itself? I don't know how you would do that with Steam, but it might be worth trying with the stand-alone free trial.
